chunks: Ali (ibn al-Hakam) from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:
I asked him about the child, the slave, and the Christian who testify with a testimony. So the Christian becomes a Muslim, would his testimony be allowed? He said: Yes.

key_terms.أَحَدِهِمَا: One of the two (referring to the 5th or 6th Imam)

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a convert from Christianity to Islam accepted in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirms the legal validity of a Christian convert's testimony, establishing that conversion to Islam fully restores their capacity to serve as a witness in Islamic jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the principle that the prior religious status does not permanently disqualify an individual, provided they embrace Islam, thereby integrating them into the community of believers for legal purposes. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of legal capacity upon conversion, distinguishing it from cases where specific disqualifications might persist.
